limitations: STRATIFICATION NOT MET: asked for 5 per class, got 13 of 25 — argswap 1, boolean 2, constant 5, drop-stmt 1, operator 4. Per-class rates are NOT comparable; the conditional rate is unaffected because it conditions on trials that happened. CORRECTED CAUSE: this was first recorded as the classes exhausting the corpus. They did not. The harness broke out of its candidate loop UNCONDITIONALLY after the first function in each file, so a file whose first function could not take the mutator was discarded whole. Measured over the same 78-file corpus: first-candidate-only yields argswap 3 / drop-stmt 3 / boolean 3, while trying until one fits yields 26 / 17 / 22. The corpus supports 17+ per class for every class. Fixed for the next run.
n=10 on the conditional. 100% is a ceiling observation, not a proven rate.
Transport quality UNMEASURED: this run predates the driver recording extraction status, so a strange model answer cannot be distinguished from a driver that mangled a conventional one.
Invalid-output cost UNMEASURED: the harness did not retain the episode, and patch_reverted is the only record of a proposal read correctly that still broke the build.

Candidate<->proposal ownership was inferred from ORDER, admitted only because segment count equalled candidate count on every trial. The next run carries candidate identity per proposal and needs no inference.
94% of all tokens are cache traffic — the harness's system prompt, not the repair.

corpus_capacity_per_class.note: Computed over examples/stdlib/*.ax + examples/*.ax with the harness's own mutators and fn_span. Does not apply the `axon check` / `failing_tests` file filters, which reduce both columns further, so these are upper bounds on each rule.
